episodes.topic: Lupita greets Jisoo at the park gate in the morning: buenos días, hola and a short reply to ¿cómo estás?
Jisoo recognizes Lupita by the park fountain in the afternoon and says buenas tardes before asking how she is.
Lupita and Jisoo say hasta mañana as they leave the park, using the bench as tomorrow's meeting point.
Everyday things at the park entrance, featuring la entrada.
Visible landmarks around the park fountain, featuring la fuente.
Things beside a park path where friends say goodbye, featuring la banca.
At a language meetup, Lupita and Jisoo read their name tags and introduce themselves with me llamo and mucho gusto.
Lupita and Jisoo set down their backpacks and ask ¿de dónde eres? They are from Mexico and Korea.
At a language class, Lupita asks what Jisoo studies and he shows her his book for learning Spanish.
Objects at a language meetup check-in table, featuring la etiqueta con el nombre.
Familiar objects in a language classroom, featuring el libro.
Items learners carry to their first class, featuring la mochila.
Jisoo misses Lupita's question about his notebook and asks ¿puedes repetir? before giving a short answer.
Lupita asks Jisoo to say a word more slowly while listening through headphones, then repeats it back.
Jisoo points to a whiteboard and asks Lupita what a written word means; she gives him the translation.
Items on a desk for writing down a repeated word, featuring el cuaderno.
Things used to listen to a recorded phrase, featuring los audífonos.
Things beside a classroom whiteboard, featuring el pizarrón.
Jisoo orders an iced coffee from Lupita using quisiera and answers a simple question about the size.
Lupita asks whether the café has oat milk; Jisoo offers regular milk as the alternative.
Jisoo orders a slice of cake, and Lupita asks if it is para aquí or para llevar.
Drinks and visible ingredients at a Mexican café, featuring el café con hielo.
Milk options and containers on a café counter, featuring la leche de avena.
Café desserts and takeaway containers, featuring el pastel.
At a fruit stall, Lupita asks ¿cuánto cuesta el kilo? and Jisoo gives a simple price in pesos.
Jisoo asks if he can pay by card for a hat, and Lupita says the market stall only takes cash.
Lupita pays for a woven bag with a bill and Jisoo gives her the change and receipt.
Fruit stall items used to weigh and price an order, featuring la báscula.
Physical payment items at a market stall, featuring la tarjeta.
Things handed over after a purchase, featuring el recibo.
Jisoo asks Lupita where the pharmacy is; go straight for one block and stop at the traffic light.
Lupita asks Jisoo how to get to the bakery; turn left at the corner and look for the sign.
Jisoo checks whether the entrance to the library is next to the newspaper stand or across the street.
Street crossing landmarks used when giving directions, featuring el semáforo.
Storefront and street-corner landmarks, featuring el letrero.
Landmarks near a public library entrance, featuring el puesto de periódicos.
Lupita invites Jisoo to a picnic on Saturday and proposes a meeting time using a las.
Jisoo cannot go to the movies on Friday; he suggests Sunday instead and Lupita agrees.
Lupita checks the hours on a museum poster and agrees with Jisoo to meet by the ticket window.
Things to pack for a Saturday picnic, featuring la canasta.
Things seen at a movie theater outing, featuring el boleto de cine.
Visible objects near a museum visit entrance, featuring la taquilla.
Jisoo asks Lupita if the bus at this stop goes to el centro and learns which route number to take.
On the bus, Lupita asks Jisoo where they get off and confirms it is the stop after the bridge.
At a station kiosk, Jisoo asks Lupita how much to load onto a transit card for two rides.
What riders see at a city bus stop, featuring la parada.
Objects inside a city bus, featuring el botón de parada.
Items used at a transit station kiosk, featuring la tarjeta de transporte.
Lupita likes a shirt but needs a different size; Jisoo looks for a medium in the same color.
Jisoo asks where the fitting room is and tells Lupita the pants fit but are too long.
Lupita returns a jacket with the tag attached and asks Jisoo if she can exchange it for a lighter one.
Common everyday shirts and tops on a clothing rack, featuring la playera.
Clothes and fixtures around a fitting room, featuring el espejo.
Items used to exchange a garment, featuring la etiqueta de precio.
Jisoo asks Lupita which vegetables to buy for salsa and checks how many tomatoes they need.
Lupita asks Jisoo to wash the vegetables while she gets a cutting board and knife.
Jisoo tastes the salsa and asks if it needs more lime; Lupita suggests a little salt first.
Produce used in a simple Mexican salsa, featuring el jitomate.
Kitchen tools for washing and chopping produce, featuring la tabla de picar.
Tabletop ingredients and utensils for seasoning salsa, featuring el limón.
Lupita sees dark clouds before a walk and asks Jisoo whether they should take an umbrella or wait.
Jisoo plans what to wear on a windy morning with Lupita and decides to bring a light sweater for later.
It starts raining before Lupita and Jisoo leave; they move their outdoor meet-up indoors and agree on a new time.
Wearable and handheld rain gear, featuring el paraguas.
Layers and accessories for a windy morning, featuring el suéter.
Familiar objects used when arriving somewhere wet, featuring el tapete.
Jisoo checks in under his last name and confirms with Lupita that his booking is for two nights.
Lupita asks Jisoo where the elevator is and confirms which floor her room is on.
Jisoo tells Lupita the room key card does not work; she offers to reactivate it and asks for his room number.
Hotel reception desk objects, featuring el mostrador.
Fixtures and signs in a hotel hallway, featuring el elevador.
Objects issued to hotel guests, featuring la tarjeta de la habitación.
Jisoo asks Lupita which tacos are mild, then orders two bistec tacos with the salsa on the side.
Lupita tells Jisoo one taco with chopped onion is missing from their order, and he politely checks with the server.
At a taquería, Jisoo asks for napkins and the check. Lupita asks to split the bill and offers to pay for the drinks.
Common taco fillings you can see at a taquería, featuring el bistec.
Things served separately with tacos, featuring la cebolla picada.
Things on a taquería dining table, featuring el servilletero.
Jisoo calls Lupita because he's running ten minutes late; she offers to wait under the clock by the station exit.
Lupita tells Jisoo her phone battery is almost dead and agrees on a fallback meeting place by a kiosk.
Their train is canceled, so Lupita and Jisoo compare taking a taxi with going tomorrow and confirm the new plan.
Landmarks people use to find one another at a train station, featuring el reloj de pared.
Phone and charging items people carry on an outing, featuring la batería portátil.
Visible objects around a taxi pickup area, featuring la cajuela.
